name: archboard init sets a repository up and hands its language servers to an agent
summary: install-skill becomes init: the skills CLI installs the skills for Codex and, when it is installed, Claude Code, and the language servers go to an agent that confirms its plan with the user, because their setup depends on the repository.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/IbGtfJE2#IFhUy8C6
changes.value: TASK-601. The run registers its checkout with repo add, as archboard init does, and lays the package itself, so a run needs no skills CLI and no network. The run's vault is the .archboard/vault that the run's checkout already holds (the run's configuration is written there before the install), so a command run in the checkout finds it without a setting. The install record holds the digest of the installed skill.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/XppR9owz#XgeEM0Pb
changes.value: TASK-601, in place of install-skill (TASK-471.03). The skills CLI (skills.sh), started by bun x, pnpm dlx or npx, installs the archboard and archboard-pr skills of the installation globally for Codex, and for Claude Code when claude is on the PATH. A person at a terminal picks the runner or skips; a caller without a terminal gets the first one found. Then the repository setup makes the vault at the root of the git checkout that holds --repo, else the working directory, and registers the checkout. Choosing and installing a language server depends on the repository, so init leaves it to an agent: at a terminal it starts Claude Code or Codex, as the person picks, with a prompt that has the agent confirm its plan first; without a terminal its answer ends with that prompt in next, for the agent that ran it. It writes nothing into the installation, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
